checks.name: raw_ip_and_same_entry_legacy_unified
checks.details: Both kernels use storage_distance_computer(index.storage), which wraps similarity distance as negative inner product; original query feeds graph distance. Both receive the same best-first HNSW route. Self-test explicitly compares IDs, distances, NDC and complete route.

checks.name: hnsw_top_m_consumption
checks.details: HNSW maxheap is drained into descending indices, giving best-first entries. Legacy mode rejects m != 3. Unified self-test uses an edgeless graph and verifies m=3/4/6/8 actual graph distance calls and returned seed IDs, rather than trusting route metadata.

checks.name: count_plain_hnsw_and_routes
checks.details: Count/plain HNSW use the same underlying IP kernel, insertion order and seed. 40 synthetic queries x 7 methods check IDs, distances, complete route including active counts/shared seed/weights/anchor. New search also checks its NDC against an independent DistanceComputer wrapper.

checks.name: pure_batch_wall_boundary
checks.details: Workspace, normalized query buffers, visited state, legacy queues, output IDs/distances and row buffers are allocated before batch(). The steady-clock boundary encloses OpenMP scheduling, route work, necessary query normalization, deduplication, search/reset and output writes; scoring, hashing, trace replay and JSON are after batch() returns. HNSW internal allocations remain timed as real routing cost.

checks.name: gt_free_real_search_and_routing
checks.details: route_online/online_query accept query/model/optional precomputed diagnostic region route, never GT. Real methods pass a null diagnostic pointer and do not inspect GT. RegionalSearch.h has no GT input or dependency.

checks.name: oracle_train_only_adapter
checks.details: GT10-to-region mass is built before timing in a separate adapter. Oracle is rejected on validation/heldout and marked non-deployment. Event-to-GT association happens only after traced search returns.

checks.name: paired_method_route_fairness
checks.details: Geometric unified/uniform/probability methods retain the same Fast anchor, default shared seed, region choice, weights and portal entries. Oracle unified/probability routes likewise match. The synthetic self-test now asserts those paired routes.

checks.name: thread_state_and_warmup
checks.details: Every worker owns search/legacy visited tables, candidate buffers, normalized storage and distance objects. Reset/advance happens per query. The fixed default warmup=128 and threads=16 exercises all active workers for the planned workloads before recorded batches. Warmup is outside recorded wall.

checks.name: preregistered_order_and_repeat_identity
checks.details: Method order is recorded before measurement, forward on even rounds and reversed on odd rounds; pilot/validation requires five rounds and heldout three. Result and complete route hashes are compared across repeated rounds, outside timing. Timing repeats are not new Recall samples.

checks.name: complete_outputs_and_trace_isolation
checks.details: Every batch writes all nq x K result IDs/distances into preallocated buffers. Aligned query-ID rows are saved for round zero, later rounds reference it. New output/parts files use exclusive creation; started/checkpoint records mark unfinished outputs. Trace replays independently after batch wall, checks IDs/NDC, then annotates GT and writes events.

required_interpretation_boundaries: Legacy parity means the old and new graph-search kernels given identical corrected best-first entries. Historical benches/test.cpp drained HNSW worst-first. Existing Fast default source is unchanged; new paired Fast20K uses corrected best-first routing and must be labelled as such, not byte-identical historical end-to-end behavior.

bench_hierarchical_eval itself checks heldout P6 freeze and oracle split restrictions, but does not validate every upstream gate. All real-data tasks must run through control/stage_run.py, whose verified source requires each earlier stage gate, validation after P5, heldout after P6 plus freeze, and taskctl supervision.
The default 128-query warmup/16-thread protocol warms active workers. Arbitrary CLI warmup values below min(threads,nq) do not guarantee that property.

Native HNSW internal allocations and built-in metric atomics remain in its actual route implementation and therefore in wall time for all compared methods; count-specific external counters are absent from plain routing.
Source/synthetic review does not establish published QPS, full-data ID/NDC parity, or algorithmic improvement. Both real workloads remain separate parent-run checks.
